parsed.attack: The realistic decay is fidelity, not interest, and it hits at the exact moment the parent is most stretched: bedtime after a bad handover, when narrating the day into a phone is the last thing that will happen. A custody log with holes is worse than no log, because opposing counsel reads the gaps as the record - so one ragged fortnight supplies a reason to stop entirely, since the evidentiary value is already dented and continuing still costs effort. And the need is episodic: orders get settled, and when the case closes the fear that drove the logging closes with it.
parsed.strongest_defence: The enforcement is external and is not the app's to lose - a family-law practitioner told this parent to keep a record, and the consequence of a gap is not a broken streak but a weaker position in front of a judge, which is the strongest retention mechanism a consumer product can borrow. The state accumulates into the one asset the user cannot afford to lose, so the renewal question is 'do I want my evidence' rather than 'did I use it enough this month', and high-conflict arrangements routinely run for years.
parsed.verdict_reason: External legal enforcement, a block that recurs every parenting day, and a record whose value rises with every entry give this a genuine reason to be opened in week two and something real to defend at the first renewal.
